# Tables

The tables here are not the final versions and I will make them using LaTeX `booktabs` instead on a separate LaTeX document.

```{r warning = F, message = F}
# Initial setup
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, 
                      fig.align='center', fig.dim=c(10, 8))

# Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(nnet)
library(stargazer)
library(broom)
library(ggpubr)
library(emmeans)
library(scales)

# Data
dat.full = readRDS(here("Objects", "dat_full.rds"))
```

We make first the population characteristics table, using `ALT3` and `GGT3` as the ALT and GGT variables. Then, we have:

- Numerical variables: `Age` and `Waist.`
- Categorical Variables: `AlcoholRisk`, `SmokingDuration`, `ExerciseGuidelines`, `Sex`, `NonShoolQuals`, `IncomeDecile`, `ALT3`, `GGT3.`

## Tables 1: Variable Definitions

| Variable | Meaning | Type / coding |
|:--------------:|:----------------------------:|:------------------------:|
| `ALT3` | Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) category | Ordered categorical factor: Low vs Borderline vs High |
| `GGT3` | Gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) category | Ordered categorical factor: Low vs Borderline vs High |
| `ExerciseGuidelines` | Whether recommended physical-activity guidelines were met | Binary factor: Yes / No |
| `Age` | Age in years | Continuous numeric |
| `Sex` | Sex | Binary factor: Female / Male |
| `Waist` | Waist circumference in cm | Continuous numeric |
| `AlcoholRisk` | Alcohol consumption risk level | Binary factor: Low risk / Medium–High risk |
| `SmokingDuration` | Duration of smoking history | Ordered categorical factor, grouped by years smoked |
| `NonSchoolQuals` | Whether a non-school educational qualification was completed | Binary factor: Yes / No |
| `IncomeDecile` | Income decile | Ordered categorical factor, deciles 1–10 |

## Tables 2: Population Characteristics Summary

Again, note that this is not the final tables, and are just drafts for the final ones on LaTeX.

```{r}
# Numerical summaries: mean, and IQR
age.summary = summary(dat.full$Age)[c(4, 2, 5)]
waist.summary = summary(dat.full$Waist)[c(4, 2, 5)]
num.summary = rbind(age.summary, waist.summary) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename("Q1" = "1st Qu.", "Q3" = "3rd Qu.")
rownames(num.summary) = c("Age", "Waist")
num.summary %>% kable(caption = "Numerical Summary")

# Categorical Summary: Variable | Class | Count | Proportion
categoricals = c("AlcoholRisk", "SmokingDuration", "ExerciseGuidelines", "Sex",
                 "NonSchoolQuals", "IncomeDecile", "ALT3", "GGT3")
cat.summary = map_df(categoricals, function(var) {
  dat.full %>%
    group_by(Class = as.character(.data[[var]])) %>%
    summarise(Count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    mutate(Variable = var, Proportion = round(Count / sum(Count), 3) * 100) %>%
    select(Variable, Class, Count, Proportion)
})

cat.summary %>% kable(caption = "Categorical Summary Table")
```

## Tables 3: Models

I think it is a bit difficult to combine the crude/main models with the interaction model, since we are comparing different things when we compare `ExerciseGuidelines`, so we split these into two tables. Additionally, I also present the table using odds ratios as well. This way, the first answers whether adjustment change the apparent exercise association; the second table (and maybe figures later on) could answer whether that association differ according to alcohol risk or smoking duration.

```{r}
# ALT Model fits
ALT.crude = nnet::multinom(formula = ALT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines,
                           data = dat.full, Hess = TRUE)
ALT.main = nnet::multinom(formula = ALT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines + Sex + AlcoholRisk + 
    SmokingDuration + NonSchoolQuals + IncomeDecile + Age + Waist,
    data = dat.full, Hess = TRUE)
ALT.int = nnet::multinom(formula = ALT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines + AlcoholRisk + 
    SmokingDuration + NonSchoolQuals + IncomeDecile + Sex + Age + Waist +
      ExerciseGuidelines : AlcoholRisk + ExerciseGuidelines : SmokingDuration,
    data = dat.full, Hess = TRUE)

# GGT Model fits
GGT.crude = nnet::multinom(formula = GGT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines,
                           data = dat.full, Hess = TRUE)
GGT.main = nnet::multinom(formula = GGT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines + Sex + AlcoholRisk + 
    SmokingDuration + NonSchoolQuals + IncomeDecile + Age + Waist,
    data = dat.full, Hess = TRUE)
GGT.int = nnet::multinom(formula = GGT3 ~ ExerciseGuidelines + AlcoholRisk + 
    SmokingDuration + NonSchoolQuals + IncomeDecile + Sex + Age + Waist +
      ExerciseGuidelines : AlcoholRisk + ExerciseGuidelines : SmokingDuration,
    data = dat.full, Hess = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Summary of just the ExerciseGuidelines coefficient + p-value
extract_exercise = function(model, model_name) {
  
  tidy(model) %>% filter(grepl("^ExerciseGuidelines", term)) %>%
    mutate(Model = model_name) %>%
    select(Model, Outcome = y.level, term, estimate, std.error, p.value)
  
}
ALT.exercise = bind_rows(extract_exercise(ALT.crude, "Crude"),
                         extract_exercise(ALT.main,  "Adjusted"))

GGT.exercise = bind_rows(extract_exercise(GGT.crude, "Crude"),
                         extract_exercise(GGT.main,  "Adjusted"))

# ALT Table
ALT.exercise.table = ALT.exercise %>% 
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3),
         p.value = case_when(p.value < 0.0001 ~ "<0.0001",
                             TRUE ~ sprintf("%.4f", p.value))) %>%
  select(Outcome, Model, estimate, p.value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = c(estimate, p.value),
              names_glue = "{Model}_{.value}")

kable(ALT.exercise.table, caption = "Exercise Guidelines and ALT Category",
      align = "c")

# GGT Table
GGT.exercise.table = GGT.exercise %>%
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3), 
         p.value = case_when(p.value < 0.0001 ~ "<0.0001",
                             TRUE ~ sprintf("%.4f", p.value))) %>%
  select(Outcome, Model, estimate, p.value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = c(estimate, p.value), 
              names_glue = "{Model}_{.value}")

kable(GGT.exercise.table, caption = "Exercise Guidelines and GGT Category",
      align = "c")
```

```{r}
# Summary using Odds Ratios
extract_exercise_OR = function(model, model_name) {
  
  tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
    filter(grepl("^ExerciseGuidelines", term)) %>%
    mutate(Model = model_name) %>%
    select(Model, Outcome = y.level, term, OR = estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 
           p.value)
  
}

# ALT
ALT.exercise.OR = bind_rows(extract_exercise_OR(ALT.crude, "Crude"),
                            extract_exercise_OR(ALT.main,  "Adjusted"))
ALT.exercise.OR = ALT.exercise.OR %>%
  mutate(`OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", OR, conf.low, conf.high),
         `p-value` = ifelse(p.value < 0.0001, "<0.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p.value)))
kable(ALT.exercise.OR, 
      caption = "Exercise Guidelines and ALT Category (Odds Ratios)", align = "c")

# GGT
GGT.exercise.OR = bind_rows(extract_exercise_OR(GGT.crude, "Crude"),
                            extract_exercise_OR(GGT.main,  "Adjusted"))
GGT.exercise.OR = GGT.exercise.OR %>%
  mutate(`OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", OR, conf.low, conf.high),
         `p-value` = ifelse(p.value < 0.0001, "<0.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p.value)))
kable(GGT.exercise.OR, 
      caption = "Exercise Guidelines and GGT Category (Odds Ratios)", align = "c")
```

The interaction table is drafted below, if needed.

```{r}
# Interactions
extract_interactions = function(model) {
  
  tidy(model) %>% filter(grepl("^ExerciseGuidelines", term)) %>%
    select(Outcome = y.level, term, estimate, std.error, p.value)
  
}

ALT.interactions = extract_interactions(ALT.int)
GGT.interactions = extract_interactions(GGT.int)

kable(ALT.interactions, digits = 3, 
      caption = "ALT Interaction Model: Exercise-Related Terms")

kable(GGT.interactions, digits = 3, 
      caption = "GGT Interaction Model: Exercise-Related Terms")
```

# Plots

## Plots 1: `ExerciseGuidelines` with `ALT3/GGT3`

To use the categorical variables as in the main model, we will set the $y$-axis as the predicted probabilities instead of the numerical values. Also the error bars are using $95\%$ confidence intervals.

```{r}
# ALT predicted probabilities
ALT.prob = emmeans(ALT.main, ~ ALT3 | ExerciseGuidelines, mode = "prob") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% rename(Outcome = ALT3) %>% mutate(Biomarker = "ALT")

# GGT predicted probabilities
GGT.prob = emmeans(GGT.main, ~ GGT3 | ExerciseGuidelines, mode = "prob") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% rename(Outcome = GGT3) %>% mutate(Biomarker = "GGT")

# Combine
biomarker.prob = bind_rows(ALT.prob, GGT.prob)
```

```{r}
# Significance tests
ALT.exercise.test = emmeans(ALT.main, ~ ExerciseGuidelines | ALT3,
                            mode = "prob") %>% 
  pairs(adjust = "none") %>% test(by = NULL, adjust = "holm") %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% rename(Outcome = ALT3) %>% mutate(Biomarker = "ALT")
GGT.exercise.test = emmeans(GGT.main, ~ ExerciseGuidelines | GGT3,
                            mode = "prob") %>%
  pairs(adjust = "none") %>% test(by = NULL, adjust = "holm") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% rename(Outcome = GGT3) %>% mutate(Biomarker = "GGT")

exercise.tests = bind_rows(ALT.exercise.test, GGT.exercise.test) %>%
  mutate(signif = case_when(p.value < 0.0001 ~ "****",
                            p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
                            p.value < 0.01 ~ "**",
                            p.value < 0.05 ~ "*",
                            TRUE ~ "ns"))

annotation.dat = biomarker.prob %>% group_by(Biomarker, Outcome) %>%
  summarise(y.position = max(upper.CL) + 0.04, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(exercise.tests %>% select(Biomarker, Outcome, signif), 
            by = c("Biomarker", "Outcome")) %>%
  mutate(group1 = "Yes", group2 = "No")

prob.plot = ggplot(biomarker.prob, aes(x = ExerciseGuidelines, y = prob)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.16) +
  stat_pvalue_manual(annotation.dat, xmin = "group1", xmax = "group2",
                     y.position = "y.position", label = "signif", 
                     tip.length = 0.01) +
  facet_grid(Biomarker ~ Outcome) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 0.9)) +
  labs(x = "Exercise Guidelines", y = "Adjusted Predicted Probability",
       title = "Adjusted ALT and GGT Category Probabilities by Exercise Status") +
  theme_classic() + theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black",
                                                      fill = NA,
                                                      linewidth = 0.4))
prob.plot
```

### Contrasts and Difference Plots

Some numerical results and tests as well for the contrasts; these test within each ALT/GGT category, how the model-adjusted predicted probability differ between `ExerciseGuidelines` is Yes and No. These are not tests of the multinomial coefficients themselves, but are a better representation of the significance stars in the plot.

```{r}
# ALT
ALT.exercise.test = emmeans(ALT.main, ~ ExerciseGuidelines | ALT3, 
                            mode = "prob") %>% pairs(adjust = "holm")
ALT.exercise.test

# GGT
GGT.exercise.test = emmeans(GGT.main, ~ ExerciseGuidelines | GGT3, 
                            mode = "prob") %>% pairs(adjust = "holm")
GGT.exercise.test
```

**Interpretation.**

- Low ALT: Yes - No = 0.000405, or about +0.04 percentage points. Essentially no difference; $p=0.9750$.
- Borderline ALT: Yes - No = 0.012353, or about +1.24 percentage points for people meeting the exercise guideline. $p=0.1766$, so no statistically significant evidence of a difference.
- High ALT: Yes - No = -0.012758, or about −1.28 percentage points. People meeting the guideline have a slightly lower adjusted predicted probability of High ALT, but $p=0.2122$, so again there is no statistically significant evidence of a difference.
- Overall: after adjustment for the covariates in ALT.main, there is no clear evidence that ALT-category probabilities differ by exercise-guideline status.

- Low GGT: Yes - No = 0.04478, so people meeting the exercise guideline have an adjusted predicted probability of Low GGT about 4.48 percentage points higher than those not meeting it. $p=0.0038$.
- Borderline GGT: difference = -0.00455, or about −0.46 percentage points. This is tiny and not statistically significant, $p=0.6303$.
- High GGT: difference = -0.04023, meaning people meeting the exercise guideline have an adjusted predicted probability of High GGT about 4.02 percentage points lower. $p=0.0037$.
- Overall: the model suggests exercise-guideline status is associated mainly with a shift from the High GGT category toward the Low GGT category, rather than much change in the Borderline category.

We can make a related difference plot for these as well, which may be better for us compared to the previous plot for interpretations.

```{r}
# Differences
ALT.diff = emmeans(ALT.main, ~ ExerciseGuidelines | ALT3, mode = "prob") %>%
  pairs(adjust = "holm") %>% confint(by = NULL, adjust = "holm") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% rename(Outcome = ALT3) %>% mutate(Biomarker = "ALT")

GGT.diff = emmeans(GGT.main, ~ ExerciseGuidelines | GGT3, mode = "prob") %>%
  pairs(adjust = "holm") %>% confint(by = NULL, adjust = "holm") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% rename(Outcome = GGT3) %>% mutate(Biomarker = "GGT")
prob.diff = bind_rows(ALT.diff, GGT.diff)

# Plot
diffs = ggplot(prob.diff, aes(x = estimate, y = Outcome)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL), height = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~ Biomarker) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted Probability Difference (Yes − No)",
       y = "Biomarker Category",
       title = "Adjusted Difference in ALT and GGT Category Probabilities") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))
diffs
```

## Interaction Plots

We plot the interaction difference plots e.g., plotting the value of $$P(\text{High}\mid\text{Exercise=Yes})-P(\text{High}\mid\text{Exercise=No})$$for each set of relevant variables.

```{r}
# Helper function
get_interaction_diff = function(model, outcome, moderator, biomarker) {
  
  specs = as.formula(paste("~ ExerciseGuidelines |", moderator, "+", outcome))
  emm = emmeans(model, specs, mode = "prob")
  
  pairs(emm, adjust = "none") %>% 
    summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95, adjust = "none") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rename(Level = all_of(moderator), Outcome = all_of(outcome)) %>%
    mutate(Biomarker = biomarker)
  
}

# Smoking
ALT.smoking.diff = get_interaction_diff(ALT.int, outcome = "ALT3",
                                        moderator = "SmokingDuration",
                                        biomarker = "ALT")
GGT.smoking.diff = get_interaction_diff(GGT.int, outcome = "GGT3", 
                                        moderator = "SmokingDuration",
                                        biomarker = "GGT")
smoking.diff = bind_rows(ALT.smoking.diff, GGT.smoking.diff)

smoking = ggplot(smoking.diff, aes(x = estimate, y = Level)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL), height = 0.12) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + facet_grid(Biomarker ~ Outcome) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted Probability Difference (Exercise Yes − No)",
       y = "Smoking Duration",
       title = "Physical Guidelines Effect Across Smoking Duration") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))
smoking
```

```{r}
# Alcohol
ALT.alcohol.diff = get_interaction_diff(ALT.int,outcome = "ALT3",
                                        moderator = "AlcoholRisk",
                                        biomarker = "ALT")
GGT.alcohol.diff = get_interaction_diff(GGT.int, outcome = "GGT3",
                                        moderator = "AlcoholRisk",
                                        biomarker = "GGT")
alcohol.diff = bind_rows(ALT.alcohol.diff, GGT.alcohol.diff)

# Plot
alc = ggplot(alcohol.diff, aes(x = estimate, y = Level)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL), height = 0.12) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + facet_grid(Biomarker ~ Outcome) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Adjusted Probability Difference (Exercise Yes − No)",
       y = "Alcohol Risk",
       title = "Physical Guidelines Effect Across Alcohol Risk") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4))
alc
```

Note that the nteraction model/test provides evidence about whether effect modification existsl the interaction-difference plots above tells us where that modification appears to occur and how large the subgroup-specific differences are.
